verdict.rationale: Sentry's own developer docs say you can run all of Sentry on your own server without paying anything, and it maintains an official minimal self-hosted setup that works out of the box for simple use cases (sentry-docs-28, sentry-docs-9). Hands-on users report self-hosted Sentry running in production and being "rock-solid once running" (sentry-comm-13), and others cite it as an escape hatch from vendor lock-in (sentry-comm-5, sentry-comm-12, sentry-comm-9). Missing for 10: the official setup is described as minimal and for simple use cases, with no documented path for scaled deployments; there is a heavy, growing infrastructure footprint (sentry-comm-1, sentry-comm-4); self-hosted releases lag SaaS launches; and licensing is source-available (BSL) rather than open source (sentry-comm-15).
